**Premier Retail Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript**

**Operator:**  
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Premier Retail Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, the Q&A session will follow the standard process: please press star then 1 on your touchtone phone to join the queue. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:**  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Premier Retail Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Alex Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer; Mike Donovan, Chief Stores Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Marketing Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

**Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:**  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report Premier Retail Inc.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Premier Retail Inc. stands as a premier brick-and-mortar retailer focused on home improvement, furniture, appliances, and daily essentials, operating more than 1,200 stores throughout North America. I'm excited to highlight our robust Q3 outcomes amid ongoing inflation, interest rates between 5.25% and 5.50%, and consumer confidence sliding to 68.7 according to the Conference Board index. These figures reflect our durable value offering and progress under our "Essentials Everywhere" omnichannel approach.

Top-line results led the way: Q3 net revenues reached $2.52 billion, climbing 8.2% year-over-year and exceeding our guidance midpoint plus consensus by 150 basis points. This extends our run of six straight quarters of growth, powered by 5.4% comparable store sales—or SSS—growth excluding fuel impacts. Traffic rose 2.8%, average ticket hit $128 with a 2.5% gain as shoppers shifted to our private-label value options amid price pressures. E-commerce now accounts for 14.2% of total sales, up from 11.8% last year, accelerated by BOPIS where 62% of digital orders were fulfilled curbside or in-store within two hours.

Stacked two-year comps advanced 10.1%, surpassing the NRF retail average of 7.2%. New stores added 220 basis points to growth, including 12 openings in Sunbelt hotspots like Texas and Florida, outperforming national averages by 15-20% in productivity.

Profitability expanded through cost discipline and supply chain gains. Gross margin grew 110 basis points to 35.2%, the strongest Q3 in five years, boosted by 320 basis points shrink reduction to 1.12% of sales via our AI EagleEye platform using computer vision and RFID to cut out-of-stocks 18% and organized retail crime 25%. Freight and LTL eased to 4.8% of COGS from 5.6%, aided by optimized Asia routes and 15% more nearshored SKUs from Mexico in "Resilient Supply Chain 2.0."

Operating income surged 22.7% to $285 million for an 11.3% margin, up 140 basis points. SG&A deleveraged 90 basis points to 16.4% via labor scheduling in our Kronos tool, lifting productivity 12% per store-hour. Adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to $410 million at 16.3% margin, rivaling Home Depot and Lowe's at 15-16%. Diluted EPS hit $1.42, up 25% and beating by $0.08, excluding a $12 million gain from divesting three Midwest stores. Free cash flow jumped 30% to $320 million, funding $150 million repurchases under our $1 billion program and a dividend increase to $0.28 per share, yielding 1.8%.

By category, hardlines like appliances, lumber, and paint fueled 55% of comp growth at +7.1% SSS. Appliances leaped 14% on energy-efficient demand for IRA rebates, partnering with Whirlpool and GE for 22% ENERGY STAR share. Softlines apparel and decor grew 2.8%, pressured by cool weather, but Hero Brands loyalty drove 9% repeats.

Regionally, Sunbelt (42% of stores) comped 8.6% on +1.2% household formation in Florida and outdoor sales +18%. Midwest was +0.4% amid flooding impacting 15 stores; Northeast +4.2% despite competitor expansions; Canada 45 stores added $180 million, +6% local currency.

These affirm our pillars: omnichannel acceleration with ship-from-store at 95% locations, +28% e-comm comps, 35% more Amazon Prime wallet share per Nielsen; store optimization with 75 NextGen remodels lifting traffic 12-15%, turns 5.8x; value innovation with private labels at 32% sales, 20-25% better margins.

Q4 guide: revenue +6-8%, comps +3.5-5%, gross 35.0-35.5%, EPS $1.35-1.45. FY comps +4-6%, $450m capex for 20 stores/100 remodels.

In short, Q3 shows our thrive in value-premium barbell retail, leading hybrid future.

We are confident in navigating challenges and creating shareholder value.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera to provide more details on our financial results.

**Alex Rivera, Chief Financial Officer:**  
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.52 billion, an 8.2% increase compared to the same period last year.

Gross margin was 35.2%, primarily driven by disciplined markdown management. Good afternoon, everyone. As we unpack our financials, let's examine markdown activity and its effect on gross margins—a vital factor in our brick-and-mortar operations where pricing and inventory productivity matter most.

In Q3, markdowns as a percentage of net sales were 11.8%, up 140 basis points from 10.4% prior year, slightly above our 11.0-11.5% guide. This stemmed from 4% higher units per store entering the quarter, mainly softlines like apparel and home, pre-buying for tariffs and volatility—similar to Macy's and Kohl's. It supported 5.4% comps (3.2% traffic, -0.4% basket), but required promotions for 5.2x turns target.

Adjusted gross margin hit 35.2%, down 110 basis points from 35.8% last year. Markdowns drove 80 basis points compression, freight 20 basis points from Red Sea issues, shrinkage 10 basis points in beauty/electronics.

By segment: Apparel (45% sales) markdowns 18.2% vs 15.9%, margins 32.1% on cool Midwest/South weather. Home & Seasonal (25%) 9.5% flat, margins 38.4% with 35% private-label Haven Home at 72% full-price. Hardlines/Essentials (30%) 6.8% vs 6.2%, margins 36.2%.

Regions: Northeast (30% stores) 10.2% markdowns, 37.1% margin on tourism. South 13.4%, 32.8% on hurricanes. West 11.5%, Midwest 12.1% on spending softness.

Mitigations: SymphonyAI dynamic pricing in 40% stores cut clearance 15%, +25 bps apparel. Manhattan WMS upgrade +12% forecasting, micro-merchandising via ShopperTrak. 75% full-price KPI, price match to 15 rivals, loyalty 62%. Omni ship-from-store 28% e-comm, +50 bps.

Q4 markdowns 10.5-11.0%, gross 35.0-35.4%; FY 35.2%, upside from private-label to 45%, 50 closures/20 urban opens.

While pressured, initiatives set re-expansion.

Operating expenses were $980 million, representing 35% of revenue, with leverage from payroll efficiencies. Good afternoon, everyone. Before segment details, note labor costs and store payroll leverage, our top SG&A controllable at 16-20% sales. Positive leverage expands margins amid wage inflation and omnichannel shifts.

Q3 store payroll $152.4 million, +4.2% YoY vs 7.8% comps, 360 bps leverage to 18.1% from 19.4%—best Q3 in five years. Stacked two-year: comps +12.5%, payroll +8.1%.

Sales per labor hour $48.20 +3.1%, 10th quarter gain on 6.2% traffic in home/apparel, private-label refresh.

Wages +5.8% to $17.45/hour, aligning NRF, down from 2022 doubles. CA/NY hikes added 80 bps; turnover 68% vs industry 75%.

Regions: Sunbelt 16.8% (-110 bps), $52.40/labor hour. Northeast 19.6% (+20 bps). Midwest 18.0%.

Initiatives: $25m Smart Labor Ecosystem. UKG scheduling 92% traffic accuracy, -12% overstaff, -22% OT, 50 bps leverage. 450 AutoStore cut BOPIS labor 40%, self-checkout 32% transactions. HomeStyle University app 65% trained, +15% ship-from-store.

H2 target 17.5-18.0%, Dynamic Zoning to 600 stores, robotic scanning. Risks: wage hikes, unions.

Q3 leverage added $18m EBITDA.

Net income was $210 million, or $1.25 per share.

We generated $350 million in cash flow from operations.

Inventory levels are currently down 14% YoY to $1.18 billion. Good afternoon, everyone. Before Q&A, deeper on inventory, key for turns, margins, cash in brick-and-mortar post-pandemic.

Ending inventory $1.18 billion, -14% from $1.37 billion Q3 last year—fourth straight decline, leanest since pre-COVID. Per sq ft -11% vs 5.4% comps.

DOH 62 from 75 (-17%), turns 5.9x from 4.9x. Apparel 55 from 68 days (+22% activewear), home 70 steady, footwear 48 from 60.

Drivers: AI Manhattan platform 85% assortments, 92% accuracy (POS, BOPIS, 3PL)—like Macy's/Target. Nearshoring 45% apparel from 28%, -22% lead times vs Red Sea +15%. VMI with VF/Tempur 98% fill, -18% inbound.

Regions: NA 72% stores -16%, Sunbelt fast turns. Europe 18% -8% on sentiment. Asia-Pac 10% -12% +15% traffic.

Markdowns 12.4% from 16.2%, +110 bps margin. Q4 -8-10% YoY, 58-60 DOH.

Stores First strategy: 28% e-comm from stores +19% YoY, $250m working capital.

Competitive moat.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in growth.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Lisa Chen, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Mike Donovan to discuss store operations, Emily Vargas to discuss marketing initiatives, and Raj Patel to talk about technology advancements.

**Lisa Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer:**  
Thank you, Alex. This quarter, we launched our expanded private-label Haven Home essentials line, which has seen strong uptake with 72% full-price sell-through and contributed to category comps exceeding 5%, particularly in kitchenware and seasonal decor bundles. We are excited about the potential of this line and other upcoming launches in activewear and eco-friendly apparel.

**Mike Donovan, Chief Stores Officer:**  
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented our accelerated remodel program, and are seeing positive results. Good afternoon, everyone. Our 1,200-store fleet drives 80%+ revenue in omnichannel world, so our remodels under 'Store of the Future' counter traffic declines of 3-5% industry-wide per Placer.ai, targeting mid-single comps via experiences/efficiencies.

Pilots in 45 urban/Sunbelt stores (Northeast, Atlanta, Phoenix, DFW) delivered 12-15% comp uplift first quarter post, +8% conversion, +6% ticket to $78, +120 bps margins to 42.5% on presentation/shrink.

FY25 $650m capex (+20%) for 225 remodels (18% fleet): 150 full at $2.8m, 75 express $1.2m. FY26 325 at $550m, 15% savings via Kimball/Shaw.

Pillars: experiential—20% more apparel modular RFID racks +22% women's conversion, AR home studios +18% attach, fresh markets. Omni: 5,000 sq ft BOPIS +30% velocity, Samsung walls/loyalty sync, NCR POS -40% lines, 65% contactless, Zebra RFID 98% accuracy -25% stockouts. Sustainability: 40% recycled, LEDs -35% energy, $15m rebates.

Regional: Midwest value layouts +9% comps, Sunbelt outdoor +25%, urban luxury pop-ups.

3-year payback, 25% IRR > Walmart 8-10%. Q3 remodeled comps +11.4% vs flat.

Hedged construction inflation, fortifies vs Amazon.

**Emily Vargas, Chief Marketing Officer:**  
Thank you, Mike. Our new "Everyday Essentials" campaign has increased brand awareness by 25%, leveraging loyalty app personalization and geofenced promotions to drive 18% repeat visits and support omnichannel adoption.

**Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer:**  
Thank you, Emily. We have invested in AI-driven demand sensing and RFID scaling with Manhattan and Zebra, which has improved inventory accuracy to 98% and fulfillment rates by 15-60% across pilots.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

**Operator:**  
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

**John Smith (JPMorgan):**  
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of softening discretionary spending trends on your sales?

**Johnathan Hale:**  
Good morning, John. Softening discretionary has hit big-ticket areas like furniture, but our essentials and private-label focus, plus omnichannel convenience, offset with consumables comps at 7% and traffic resilience in value tiers. We're gaining share there.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

**Mike Johnson (Goldman Sachs):**  
Thanks. What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

**Alex Rivera:**  
Thank you, Mike. Good afternoon, everyone. As Q3 comps hit 5.4% with 2.8% traffic and 2.6% AUR, here's our Q4 and FY2025 outlook amid cautious consumers, leaning on omnichannel and optimizations.

Q4 comps 2.5-4.5%, traffic flat to +1.5%, AUR +2.0-3.0%. Matches promo cadence, better inventory -8% YoY for full-price. U.S. 3.0-5.0% Sunbelt strength +12% traffic remodels/BOPIS; Midwest 1.0-3.0% big-ticket softness; int'l Canada/UK 1.5-3.5% holiday, -50 bps FX.

FY2025 3.0-5.0%, accelerating FY24 2.8-3.8%. Store 2.0 remodels 250 with curbside/RFID +15% conversion. Consumables 5-7% private-label EverFresh 80% stores; apparel/home 2.5-4.5% AI loyalty +25% users +18% repeats.

1,800-store optimized fleet (50 closures/30 urban), 60% omni sales, BOPIS/ship 28% +6 pts. Shopify POS/dynamic pricing +150 bps margin. Domestic sourcing 45% apparel.

Risks: 3.2% CPI, wages 15 states, discounters, weather +/-50-100 bps, geopolitics. Private-label 35%, $1.2b capex conviction. $500m buybacks, 2.1% yield.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Lisa Brown with Barclays. Please go ahead.

**Lisa Brown (Barclays):**  
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

**Johnathan Hale:**  
Absolutely, Lisa. Nearshoring to 45% apparel from Mexico/Central America cut lead times 22%, VMI with partners ensured 98% fill rates, and omni store fulfillment dodged disruptions like Red Sea, maintaining turns at 5.9x.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

**David Lee (Morgan Stanley):**  
What is the impact from the store remodel program?

**Johnathan Hale:**  
Great question, David. Remodels are delivering 12-15% comp lifts, margin gains, and traffic conversion boosts, with ROI exceeding 25% IRR, positioning high-density stores as omni hubs.

**Operator:**  
[Optional: More Analyst Questions] Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

**Sarah Jenkins (Goldman Sachs):**  
Thanks, good afternoon, team. I wanted to dive deeper into your strategies for inventory optimization, especially given supply chain headwinds and e-comm pressures from Amazon. Specifics, impacts, regional?

**Alex Rivera:**  
Absolutely, Sarah, core to our playbook at Premier Retail Inc. Inventory carrying costs hit 28% COGS industry-wide per NRF, worsened by Red Sea +40% freight Q3. Optimization drives 15% EBITDA target FY24.

Four pillars across 1,200 stores: turnover 5.8x from 4.2x FY22, DIO 63 -18%, excess $185m -27%, $220m capital freed.

Pillar 1: HomeAI Predict with Blue Yonder/Snowflake, 92% accuracy vs 78% legacy, 15 signals (Google Trends kitchen remodels, weather, CPI). Holiday small appliances stockouts 3.2% from 12%, $50-100 lost/incident McKinsey.

Pillar 2: 65% JIT replen, RFID 80% SKUs, IoT shelves 400 stores, VMI P&G/Whirlpool 40% FMCG. Safety stock 1.5 weeks A-items, fill 97.5%, obsolescence -22%, seasonal markdowns 4% from 15%.

Pillar 3: Culls 12% low-turn SKUs <2x, private CoreHome 28% sales 7.2x. Localization: Northeast cold essentials +15% DIO -22%; Southwest HVAC/grills +31% turns vs 14% avg.

Pillar 4: BOPIS/ship-from-store 35% sales +13 pts, Store-to-Door Manhattan WMS 70% orders <50 miles <2 days +8% traffic. Port strikes pivoted 25% West to East, 98% in-stock.

Regions: Midwest VMI -19% DIO trucking +15%; urban coasts 6.5x+ turns. Pilots blockchain IBM, $75m DC automation, +10% turns FY25.

Net inventory 22% sales vs peers 28%, 12% comps support, ahead Target/Walmart, mid-teens ROIC.

**Operator:**  
Thank you. That concludes the Q&A portion.

**Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:**  
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

**Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:**  
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
